sections.name: settings
sections.notes: All active writable settings emitted by the current Smithproxy saver are typed and editable with ranges aligned to the pinned upstream schema. Non-QUIC worker pools accept non-negative counts and defer the target-specific hardware ceiling to authoritative Smithproxy validation; QUIC accepts -1, 0, or 1. Non-canonical legacy live worker values remain readable without being resubmitted when unrelated settings change. OCSP and CRL status TTLs remain visible but read-only because upstream marks them VALUE_NONE. Integer quotas accept the full lossless JSON range. HTTP API and webhook identities, endpoints, bind targets, administration identity, filesystem paths, credentials, API keys, syslog targets, filename components, and rating keys use write-only replace/clear controls. Deprecated thread-spray tuning keys are accepted and ignored by Smithproxy and are intentionally not exposed.

sections.name: debug
sections.notes: Global debug flags and the current per-module boolean, integer, and bounded string logging overrides are typed and editable. Module names are constrained to draft-path-safe identifiers.

sections.name: address_objects
sections.notes: The pinned Smithproxy schema supports CIDR and FQDN address objects only; both are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. CIDR inputs show their normalized address range, while FQDN inputs provide an explicit best-effort DNS evaluation from the GUI core without contacting the resolved targets or changing the draft. A live object can prefill an explicit copy from its persistent and pending values without baking in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed structural deletion is available only for objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: port_objects
sections.notes: Port ranges are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates ascending bounded ranges; a live range can prefill an explicit copy from its persistent and pending values without baking in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy/routing references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: proto_objects
sections.notes: Protocol identifiers are represented by typed edit and structural create drawers. Creation validates unique protocol numbers in the Smithproxy-supported range 1-255; a live object can prefill an explicit copy but requires a new number before saving and never bakes in temporary augment overlays. Confirmed deletion is limited to objects without live or pending policy references and without pending field edits. Visible unused address, port, and protocol objects can be staged for deletion together in one confirmed atomic batch using the same dependency guards. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: detection_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current detection-profile saver are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: captures
sections.notes: All active capture fields are typed and editable. Numeric quotas accept the full lossless JSON integer range supported by the GUI transport. Paths, filename components, destination addresses, and interface names use write-only replace/clear controls and remain redacted in draft responses.

sections.name: content_profiles
sections.notes: Content controls and nested rule action metadata are typed. Complete parent profiles support structural creation and safe duplication of non-sensitive persistent and pending values; session filters, nested rules, and augment overlays are explicitly excluded from copies. Session filters and rule match/replacement expressions remain server-side and use write-only rotation. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup. Nested rules support ordered structural creation, confirmed deletion, and first/before/last moves when the reviewed structural capability is available; their parent editor presents the effective draft order, labels pending moves and deletes, and permits create or move references to earlier same-parent pending creates. Accepted write-only create values are cleared from the editor and must be re-entered before updating a pending create operation.

sections.name: tls_ca
sections.notes: Authority names and path posture are exposed. Authorities support structural creation, safe name duplication from persistent and pending values without augment overlays, and confirmed deletion, with pending deletion labeled in the trust-asset list. Filesystem paths use write-only controls, are excluded from copies, are cleared after acceptance, remain redacted in draft responses, and must be re-entered before a pending create can be updated.

sections.name: tls_profiles
sections.notes: All active fields saved by the current Smithproxy TLS profile schema are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays. SNI bypass expressions support write-only replace or clear, never cross the browser boundary, and are explicitly excluded from copies. Updating a pending create requires explicit bypass-list re-entry. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: ssh_profiles
sections.notes: All active SSH profile fields are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays; host-key paths are write-only, remain redacted, and are explicitly excluded from copies. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: alg_dns_profiles
sections.notes: The current DNS ALG profile schema is represented by typed edit, complete structural create, and safe persistent-plus-pending duplicate drawers that exclude augment overlays. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: routing
sections.notes: All active fields emitted by the current routing-profile saver are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays, with bounded unique destination lists. Address and port references resolve current draft-visible names while preserving stable live entity IDs. Stable unreferenced profiles support confirmed structural deletion individually or through filtered atomic cleanup.

sections.name: policy
sections.notes: All active policy fields returned by the snapshot contract are represented by typed edit and ordered structural create drawers. The obsolete auth_profile value remains readable only for legacy compatibility and is never shown, copied, created, or edited. Empty source, source-port, destination, and destination-port selectors preserve Smithproxy wildcard semantics. New action, NAT, and feature writes are constrained to the pinned Smithproxy enums; non-canonical legacy live values remain readable and can be migrated without resubmitting them when another field changes. References resolve live entities by their current draft-visible names and named objects or profiles created earlier in the same workspace draft; pending creates reopen their structural drawer and pending renames retain the stable live entity ID. Ordered creates and moves may target earlier pending policies through transaction-scoped client identifiers while use-before-create choices remain unavailable. Existing policies support optimistic first, before, and last move operations; restoring the original position removes the pending move. Selected live policies can move first or last in one atomic batch while preserving their internal order and avoiding no-op drafts. Confirmed single or selected-policy structural deletion is staged atomically and rejects conflicting pending field edits, structural operations, and removal of a position anchor used by another pending policy. Structural operations remain capability-gated on stable entity IDs.

sections.name: starttls_signatures
sections.notes: All active signature metadata and ordered flow controls are typed. Parent metadata and the required first flow step support atomic structural creation, safe duplication of persistent and pending non-sensitive values without augment overlays, and linked removal with one draft version increment. Copies require a new first matcher expression and explicitly omit additional flow steps. Existing signatures support confirmed structural deletion and label that state in the trust-asset list. Matcher expressions remain server-side and support write-only replacement. Stable flow steps support ordered structural creation, confirmed deletion, and first/before/last moves when the reviewed structural capability is available; their parent editor presents the effective draft order, labels pending moves and deletes, and permits create or move references to earlier same-parent pending creates. Accepted write-only create values are cleared from the editor and must be re-entered before updating a pending create operation.

sections.name: script_profiles
sections.notes: All active script-profile fields are typed, editable, structurally creatable, and safely duplicable from persistent and pending values without augment overlays; executable paths are write-only, remain redacted, and are explicitly excluded from copies. sections.name: auth_profiles
sections.notes: Legacy authentication profiles are parsed defensively so old configurations remain readable, but they are not shown, created, referenced, or edited by the GUI. Their current Smithproxy runtime behavior is obsolete and effectively a no-op. Identity matching will return only with a reviewed policy-level model; the GUI does not advertise the deprecated profile-level identity mechanism.
